waves.goal: Phase-0 module contract v2 (A16): deliver every module-facing name, signature and decentralised registration point (module metadata, statuses/reason codes, confidence labels, result helpers, ctx.http/dns/net/data/keys/quota/org helpers, body-error classification, sanitizer schemas, provider/vocab/pivot/noise/dataset/rule/spec/notice fragments, entity types, test kit and registry contract test) with thin-but-working implementations, migrate the four reference modules, and freeze docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md as contract v2. The existing suite stays green (only assertions whose behaviour the binding rules change are updated, by the package that owns the test file). INTRA-WAVE PROTOCOL (applies to every wave; critical here because WP01-WP06 build on each other's new names): (1) each package first lands an importable skeleton of its whole public_api (exact module paths, names and signatures from this plan, minimal working behaviour, no import cycles - a module that would close a cycle imports its sibling lazily inside the function) before deeper work, so siblings code against real names in the shared tree; (2) a package's own tests rely only on sibling names listed in this plan's public_api and use local stubs/fakes for sibling behaviour that is not final yet; (3) WP06 is the wave-1 integrator: after the siblings report done it runs the whole suite, fixes glue in files it owns, reports defects to the owning package and marks docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md FROZEN only on the green integrated tree; (4) the tree stays importable and green on Python 3.10 until WP29 raises requires-python to 3.11 (AR23): tomllib is imported lazily, JSON works everywhere and a .toml file on 3.10 gives a clear error.

packages.title: Result model v2: statuses, reason codes, confidence labels, deterministic ids, rule API, vocabulary fragments, TLP and ATT&CK index
packages.spec:
Extend (do not rewrite) the result model so every result-side name of contract v2 exists (module_author_contract sections 3-5, 14, 16).
1. v3lum/core/models.py.
 a) Status: add QUOTA = 'quota'; keep the 8 existing values and strings unchanged.
 b) REASON_CODES: dict[str, Status] holding exactly the A3 canonical codes (SKIPPED: not_default, demoted, licence, tlp, tier, privacy, own_asset, opsec, authorization, scope, egress_country, deadline, policy, config, not_applicable; NEEDS_KEY: needs_key; UNAVAILABLE: package, dataset, offline; QUOTA: quota; RATE_LIMITED: rate_limited; BLOCKED: hostile_host, circuit, challenge, geo_block, login_wall; ERROR: timeout, sanitizer, error). STOP_REASONS = frozenset({'request_cap','deadline','quota','rate_limited','cancelled'}). DEFAULT_REASON = {SKIPPED:'not_applicable', NEEDS_KEY:'needs_key', UNAVAILABLE:'offline', QUOTA:'quota', RATE_LIMITED:'rate_limited', BLOCKED:'challenge', ERROR:'error'}. status_for(code) -> Status (ValueError on unknown code); valid_reason(status, code) -> bool.
 c) Confidence(str, Enum) CONFIRMED='confirmed', PROBABLE='probable', POSSIBLE='possible' with .weight (1.0/0.7/0.4), .stix (90/70/40), .rank (2/1/0), .lower(), .higher(); Confidence.from_value(value: float|str|Confidence) (float >= 0.85 -> confirmed, >= 0.55 -> probable, else possible; strings case-insensitive by value or name). CONFIDENCE_TABLE: the documented label/weight/stix table (single source used by P302/P303).
 d) finding_id(module, entity_key, title, key='') = sha256('|'.join([module, entity_key, title, key]).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:16]; correlation_id(rule, entity_keys, key='') = sha256(('rule|' + rule + '|' + ','.join(sorted(entity_keys)) + '|' + key).encode()).hexdigest()[:16] (AR09).
 e) Finding: keep the existing fields and their order; add confidence_label: Confidence | None (derived from confidence when None), criterion: str = '', source: str = '' (registry source id), observed_first: str | None = None, observed_last: str | None = None (ISO-8601 provider timestamps), attack: list[str], key: str = '', suppressed_by: list[dict] ({'rule','reason'}), ownership: str = '' ('own_asset'|'third_party'|''). id defaults to '' and ensure_id() fills finding_id(...) once module and entity are known (ModuleResult.finding calls it; the engine calls it again after forcing f.module). downgrade(rule, reason) lowers the label one level (floor possible), appends to suppressed_by and sets criterion to '<LABEL> - <reason>' (e.g. 'POSSIBLE - on warninglist <name>') keeping the previous criterion after ' | '; upgrade(independent_families, rule, reason) raises one level only when independent_families >= 2. to_dict() adds confidence_label, criterion, source, observed_first, observed_last, attack, key, suppressed_by, ownership; Finding.from_dict(d) accepts stored v1 dicts (no label -> from_value(confidence); 12-char ids kept).
 f) Pivot: confidence accepts a float or a label (stored as float via weight for labels); property confidence_label.
 g) ModuleResult: add reason_code: str = '', partial: bool = False, stop_reason: str = '', tlp: str = '', hosts: dict[str, int], datasets: list[dict], redacted_fields: list[str]. Builders: finding(title, severity='info', description='', *, confidence=0.8, criterion='', data=None, tags=(), references=(), source='', observed_first=None, observed_last=None, attack=(), key='') -> Finding; pivot(etype, value, relation, *, confidence=0.9, expand=True, note='') (float or label); attr(key, value); link(label, url) keeps only http/https URLs (AR13); mark(status, error='', *, reason_code='') -> self (empty reason_code -> DEFAULT_REASON for non ok/empty statuses; ValueError when valid_reason is False); stop(stop_reason) -> self (partial=True; ValueError outside STOP_REASONS); presence(state, *, marker='', url='', checked_at=None, source='') with state in {'found','absent','unknown'} stores attribute 'presence' = {'state','marker','url','checked_at','source'} and refuses 'absent' without marker or url (P328 cond 4); set_marking(tlp) keeps the highest TLP (tlp.parse). to_dict() adds reason_code, partial, stop_reason, tlp, hosts, datasets, redacted_fields.
 h) Strict contract mode: when vocab.strict_enabled() (env V3LUM_STRICT == '1', set by tests/conftest.py) finding() raises ContractViolation for severity >= LOW without criterion and for non-http(s) references, link() raises for non-http(s) URLs, presence('absent') without evidence raises, and attr()/finding(tags)/pivot(relation) raise UnknownVocab (subclass of ContractViolation) for names outside the merged vocabulary. Non-strict mode never raises: a missing criterion becomes 'unspecified' and unknown names are kept, both logged once per (module, name) on logger 'v3lum.contract'.
 i) collect_results(): context manager (contextvars) to which every ModuleResult created inside registers (ModuleResult.__post_init__); the engine uses it to recover the result a module was building when it raised RequestCapReached/Cancelled/QuotaExceeded/RateLimited.
 j) Correlation: id via correlation_id in __post_init__ when empty (from entities and key); add criterion='', confidence_label=None (derived), attack=[], references=[], version='1', why='', key='', suppressed_by=[]; to_dict() adds them.
2. v3lum/core/vocab.py: keep ATTRIBUTES/TAGS/RELATIONS (core); add core names: attributes presence, sightings, is_sinkhole, is_parked, intercepted_by, generic_address; tags own_asset, third_party, hosted_on_legit_platform, sinkhole, parked, benign_scanner, recipient_token, version_inferred, high_collision, weak_signal, verified_fi, unknown_operator; relations similar_to, same_m365_tenant. Load fragments v3lum/data/vocab/*.json (schema 'v3lum.vocab/1'; names ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$; non-empty descriptions) once (cached), core first, then files sorted by name; a re-declared name merges (first description wins) and is reported by redeclarations() -> list[(kind, name, file)]; malformed files/entries are reported by errors() -> list[str] (never raise). API: attributes(), tags(), relations() (merged dicts), is_known_attribute/is_known_tag/is_known_relation (merged), check(kind, name) ('attribute'|'tag'|'relation'; raises UnknownVocab only in strict mode), strict_enabled(), errors(), redeclarations(), reload() (tests). README.md documents the fragment format.
3. v3lum/core/tlp.py (new): class TLP(IntEnum) CLEAR=0, GREEN=1, AMBER=2, AMBER_STRICT=3, RED=4 with .value_str ('clear','green','amber','amber+strict','red'), .label ('TLP:CLEAR' ... 'TLP:AMBER+STRICT'), .file_tag ('TLP-AMBER+STRICT'), .color (FIRST TLP 2.0 hex on black: CLEAR #FFFFFF, GREEN #33FF00, AMBER #FFC000, AMBER_STRICT #FFC000, RED #FF2B2B). parse(value) accepts the five values, 'TLP:' prefixes, 'amber_strict'/'amber-strict' and 'white' (-> CLEAR), case-insensitive; ValueError otherwise. TLP_VALUES = ('clear','green','amber','amber+strict','red'). highest(*values) -> TLP. max_tlp(disclosure, tier, *, publishes_queries, reuses_queries) -> TLP | None per P332 cond 7: publishes_queries -> None; disclosure 'none'/'internal' -> RED; 'target' -> AMBER; 'third_party': trusted -> AMBER_STRICT, community -> AMBER, unknown or reuses_queries -> GREEN. max_tlp_for_target(own_asset_verified, third_party_hosted) -> RED only when verified and not third_party_hosted, else AMBER.
4. v3lum/core/attack.py (new): Technique(id, name, stix_id, revoked, deprecated, replaced_by); loads every v3lum/data/attack/*.json (schema 'v3lum.attack_index/1': {'version', 'techniques': {id: {'name','stix_id','revoked','deprecated','replaced_by'}}}), merged (first wins). API lookup(tid), is_valid(tid) (known, not revoked/deprecated), canonical(tid) (follows replaced_by chains, e.g. T1656 -> T1684.001), validate(ids) -> list[str] errors (unknown, or revoked without replacement), stix_id(tid) -> str|None, errors(). Ship v3lum/data/attack/core_min.json with T1566, T1566.001, T1566.002, T1684.001 (name as given by the P292 dataset when available, else 'Impersonation: ...' placeholder documented) and T1656 (revoked, replaced_by T1684.001). Packs and the P292 batch add their own fragment files; nobody edits core_min.json after this wave.
5. v3lum/core/correlate.py: RuleInfo gains version='1', code='' (e.g. 'CR27'), severity='info', criterion='', references=(), attack=(), false_positives='', fixtures=(), kind='python', legacy=False, takes_context=False. @rule(rule_id, title, description='', *, version='1', code='', severity='info', criterion='', references=(), attack=(), false_positives='', fixtures=()) - the existing two-argument form keeps working; a rule function declaring three positional parameters receives rctx. LEGACY_RULES = frozenset({'multi_source_malicious','shared_infrastructure','seeds_linked','username_reuse','breach_and_infostealer','young_domain','exploitable_exposure','high_signal_tags'}) (exempt from the fixture requirement until replaced; RuleInfo.legacy=True). RuleContext dataclass (now: datetime, org: OrgProfile|None = None, options: ScanOptions|None = None, providers: ProviderRegistry|None = None, settings: Config|None = None, meta: dict = {}). run_rules(graph, results, only=None, *, rctx=None): unchanged dedupe/sort semantics, deterministic correlation ids, rule version stamped on each Correlation, ATT&CK ids canonicalised with attack.canonical. Registration validates attack ids (attack.validate) and records failures in RULE_ERRORS[rule_id]. rules_listing() -> list[dict] (id, code, version, title, severity, criterion, attack, legacy, kind, fixtures) for `v3lum rules`. register_compiler(kind, fn) hook: load_rules() loads v3lum/data/rules/*.json|*.toml only for kinds with a registered compiler (P301, wave 4).
6. v3lum/core/graph.py: Node gains ownership='', criticality='', tlp='', path_confidence=1.0, noise_kind='', tags: set[str] (entity-level tags set by the engine), add_tag(tag), tagged(*tags) (entity tags or finding tags); Edge gains property confidence_label; to_dict() emits the new fields; Graph.from_dict(d) rebuilds a graph from a stored case dict or a 'v3lum.graph_fixture/1' document (attributes as lists of {value, source}; findings via Finding.from_dict; unknown keys ignored).
7. v3lum/core/sanitize.py (new, thin; WP09 completes it in wave 2 without renaming): SanitizerSchema(source_id, keep: tuple[str, ...], notes=''); register_schema(source_id, *, keep, notes='') (keep paths: dotted keys, '[]' for list elements, '*' for any key); schema_for(source_id) -> SanitizerSchema|None (registered schemas first, else providers.registry().source(source_id).sanitizer); apply_schema(obj, schema) -> (kept_obj, redacted_paths); sanitize_body(source_id, content: bytes, content_type: str) -> bytes|None (JSON bodies filtered by the schema; non-JSON or no schema -> None meaning 'do not cache'); mask_secret(raw, kind='') -> {'type','preview','sha256'} (preview = first 4 + '…' + last 4; '****' when shorter than 12); drop_combos(text) -> str (removes email:password and user:pass@host combos keeping the e-mail); SECOND_NET_FIELDS (P145 cond 4 names); sanitize_result(res, module_cls) -> ModuleResult: for sensitive modules apply each source schema to res.raw and drop SECOND_NET_FIELDS keys (case-insensitive, nested) in raw, attributes and findings.data; for every module apply drop_combos to every string value; record res.redacted_fields; SanitizerError on internal failure.
8. v3lum/core/engine.py (thin integration only; WP08 does the deep changes): run_module(cls, entity, case_dir=None, *, run=None) builds ctx = runtime.context(cls, options, case_dir, run=run) and runs the module inside models.collect_results(); outcome mapping per module_author_contract section 3 (QuotaExceeded/RateLimited with collected data -> partial OK/EMPTY with stop_reason 'quota'/'rate_limited'; RequestCapReached -> partial stop 'request_cap'; Cancelled -> partial stop runtime.cancel_reason or 'cancelled'; Blocked keeps exc.reason_code; AuthRequired -> NEEDS_KEY for modules with requires_keys/optional_keys else BLOCKED 'challenge'; PolicyError -> SKIPPED exc.reason_code; ConfigError -> SKIPPED 'config'; DeadlineExceeded -> ERROR 'timeout'; DatasetUnavailable -> UNAVAILABLE 'dataset'; OfflineError -> UNAVAILABLE 'offline'; other errors -> ERROR 'error' with traceback in raw as today); every error string passes redact.redact_text. After the run: res.hosts = dict(ctx.http.hosts); res.datasets = list(ctx.data.used); f.ensure_id() for every finding; sanitize.sanitize_result applied (any exception -> res.raw = None, status ERROR, reason_code 'sanitizer'). select() returns blocked tuples (cls, status, reason, reason_code) using module.readiness_check (callers inside engine.py updated); an exhausted daily_quota gives QUOTA 'quota' (was RATE_LIMITED); TLP:RED with shares_input gives SKIPPED 'tlp'. Coverage entries record reason_code; _STATUS_RANK gains 'quota'. _finish passes RuleContext(now=runtime.now(), org=runtime.org, options=self.options, providers=runtime.providers, settings=runtime.config, meta=runtime.meta) to run_rules. NO_AUTO_EXPAND is imported from v3lum.core.entities (engine.NO_AUTO_EXPAND kept as an alias).
9. Review additions (contract v2, frozen with the rest of wave 1): (a) Finding.override: dict | None = None ({analyst, label, severity, verdict, note, at, auto: {label, severity, criterion}}) and Finding.apply_override(*, label=None, severity=None, verdict=None, analyst='', note='', at='') which sets confidence_label/severity and keeps the automatic values under override['auto']; downgrade(rule, reason, *, to=None) lowers one level or straight to the given label (to=Confidence.POSSIBLE for the warninglist/sinkhole/generic-address suppressions); downgrade() and upgrade() never cross an analyst decision: on an overridden finding they change nothing and only append {'rule', 'reason', 'blocked_by': 'analyst'} to suppressed_by (P322 cond 3/5, P258 cond 3); to_dict()/from_dict() carry override. (b) Core vocabulary also gains the finding tag context_only ('shown as context, never scored as exposure': third-party breach context, generic/role/test addresses, anonymity-network membership; A4 BR6/BR9, P146 cond 2/5-7, P171 cond 7) and the attribute watch_hits (list of {name, registrable_domain, serial, cert_sha256, issuer, not_before, source} reported by modules tagged watch_source for `v3lum watch`, A14/P030). (c) @rule duplicate ids: a non-legacy rule supersedes a LEGACY_RULES rule registered under the same id whatever the import order (the legacy one is dropped and listed in RULE_REPLACED); any other duplicate id is a RULE_ERRORS entry (WP23 keeps the ids multi_source_malicious/exploitable_exposure while WP22 removes the legacy versions in the same wave). (d) Rule-fixture harness (moved here from WP06): correlate.load_graph_fixture(path) -> GraphFixture(graph, results, rctx, expect) for 'v3lum.graph_fixture/1' (Graph.from_dict, Finding.from_dict, a RuleContext whose now is the fixture's 'now' and whose org is orgprofile.OrgProfile.from_dict(fixture['org_profile'])); tests/test_rule_fixtures.py is parametrized over tests/fixtures/rules/<rule_id>/{positive,negative}_*.json and runs correlate.run_rules(graph, results, only={rule_id}, rctx=rctx): positive -> at least expect.min (default 1) and at most expect.max (when given) correlations of that rule, matching expect.severity/confidence_label when given; negative -> none; tests/fixtures/rules/README.md documents the format (module_author_contract section 16); tests.fakes.graph_fixture (WP06) is a thin wrapper. (e) Interim A16 BR5 guard until WP08 replaces selection with policy.decide: Engine.select runs modules with disclosure in {'third_party', 'internal', 'target'} only when selected explicitly (options.include) or with options.include_disabled; otherwise SKIPPED 'not_default' ('source modules are opt-in until the policy gate lands (A16)'), so no source module merged by a batch is default-enabled before P145/P327/P377 are merged. (f) ModuleResult.source_status(source_id, status, *, reason_code='', reason='') -> self records per-feed outcomes of aggregator modules in res.source_statuses: dict[str, dict] ({status, reason_code, reason}; status and code validated like mark(); source_id must be one of the module's sources) - e.g. a feed that was blocked or rate limited while the others answered; to_dict() adds source_statuses (A1 BR10, P377 cond 6, P328 cond 2). (g) Timeline attributes are data: the vocab fragment schema gains an optional section "timeline": {attribute name: timeline label} (the attribute must exist in the merged vocabulary); vocab.timeline_attributes() returns the core set (today's engine._DATE_ATTRS: created, updated, expires, first_seen, last_seen, opened, archive_first, cert_not_after) merged with the fragments, and engine.build_timeline uses it instead of the hard-coded dict (_DATE_ATTRS kept as an alias of the core set), so packs and batches add dated facts such as first_seen_breach (P146 cond 10) without editing engine.py. (h) res.hosts merges ctx.http.hosts with the run's core DoH scope (ctx.doh.hosts, WP06), so the A8 disclosure ledger lists the DNS resolvers that received the value; DoH stays uncounted for max_requests and quotas.

packages.spec:
Implement module_author_contract sections 1, 2, 10, 11 and 13.
1. v3lum/core/module.py - Module ClassVars v2 exactly as in module_author_contract section 1 (names, types, defaults, allowed values). Constants: TERMS = ('open','key-terms','license','noncommercial','unknown'); DISCLOSURES = ('none','internal','third_party','target'); RUN_ON = ('any','seeds','own_assets','own_assets_only'); ACCESS_MODELS (7 values) and ACCESS_LABELS (plain words: 'free, no key, unlimited', 'free, no key, limited', 'free key, limited', 'free key, unlimited', 'paid only', 'internal platform', 'offline'); RESERVED_TAGS; MUST_DECLARE = ('terms','opsec','disclosure','hosts'); MUST_DECLARE_NETWORKED = ('max_requests','expected_latency'); DERIVED = ('trust_tier','providers','upstream_families','reliability','sensitive','publishes_queries','reuses_queries','fetches_target','shares_input','max_tlp','access_label','terms_sources'); REMOVED = ('user_agent','shares_input'); OPTIONAL_PACKAGES = {'phonenumbers':'full','dns':'full','PIL':'full','pypdf':'full','socks':'full','websocket':'watch','yaml':'yaml'}; CEILINGS = {'light_max_rps': 1.0, 'active_max_rps': 10.0}; BENIGN_VALUES (section 1 list, keyed by EntityType); HealthCheck dataclass; RegistrationError(ValueError); Readiness dataclass. 'Declared' means present in the class's own __dict__ or in the __dict__ of a base class other than Module (compiled specs and mixins count).

packages.title: HTTP and network contract: body-error classification, redaction, own redirect loop, provider profiles, caps, deadlines, thin socket connector
packages.spec:
Implement module_author_contract section 7 plus the client internals other packages build on.
1. File split (compatibility kept): HttpCache moves to v3lum/core/cache.py and HostLimiter to v3lum/core/limiter.py; v3lum/core/http.py re-exports both. v3lum/core/clock.py (new): Clock protocol (now() -> aware UTC datetime, monotonic() -> float, sleep(seconds) -> None), SystemClock, SYSTEM_CLOCK.
2. Exceptions in http.py: HttpError(message, status=0, url='', body='', reason_code='error') (message/url redacted); RateLimited(HttpError) reason_code 'rate_limited'; AuthRequired(HttpError); Blocked(HttpError) reason_code in {challenge, geo_block, login_wall, circuit, hostile_host} (default challenge); QuotaExceeded(HttpError) 'quota'; NetworkError; OfflineError(NetworkError); DeadlineExceeded(NetworkError); Cancelled(Exception); RequestCapReached(Exception); PolicyError(Exception) with .reason_code (default 'policy'; also 'scope', 'tlp', 'egress_country'); ConfigError(Exception).
3. Classification (P321): Classification(status, reason_code, reason, marker_id) and classify(resp, *, markers=(), keyless=False) -> Classification|None evaluated in this order: (1) module+provider error_markers (json_path/equals, or regex over the first 64 KB of text; optional statuses and final_url_regex) -> maps_to with reason_code default blocked->'challenge', rate_limited->'rate_limited', quota->'quota', error->'error'; (2) final URL: path or URL matching /login, /accounts/login, /signin, /authwall, linkedin.com/authwall, instagram.com/accounts/login, facebook.com/login -> blocked 'login_wall'; '/blockme.html' -> blocked 'challenge'; (3) geo-block: CloudFront 403 'The request could not be satisfied', Akamai 'Reference #' access-denied pages, HTTP 451 -> blocked 'geo_block' (reason ends with 'needs egress_country / see v3lum doctor --egress'); (4) strong markers (existing list + AWS WAF 'aws-waf-token'/'awswaf', PerimeterX '_pxhd'/'px-captcha', Vercel 'vercel security checkpoint', DDoS-Guard, Incapsula) -> blocked 'challenge', on any status; (5) weak markers (existing captcha words, 'challenge-platform', 'verify you are human') only on error statuses -> blocked 'challenge'; (6) 429 -> rate_limited; 430 -> blocked 'challenge' ('provider blacklisted this egress IP'); (7) keyless and 403 without markers -> blocked 'challenge' ('HTTP 403 for a keyless source: could not verify'). Never yields an empty/absent result. Reasons name the provider (e.g. 'HackerTarget: daily quota exhausted (API count exceeded)'). Header comment and the notice fragment v3lum/data/notices/maigret_sherlock_markers.json attribute maigret COMMON_ERRORS and sherlock WAFHitMsgs (MIT); no bypass helpers ported, no bypass hints in messages. block_reason(status, headers, body) stays as a compatibility wrapper.
4. Response: existing positional constructor kept (status, url, headers, content, elapsed=0.0, from_cache=False, truncated=False, history=[]); new trailing fields fetched_at='' (ISO UTC; cache row time on hits), request_url='', host='', source='', classification=None. raise_for_status() raises by classification first (Blocked/RateLimited/QuotaExceeded/HttpError with its reason_code), then by status as today.
5. HttpClient (existing keyword arguments kept) gains: providers (default providers.registry()), settings (Config or mapping: user_agent, contact_email, ua_light, ca_bundle, cache_max_age_days, retention_days), transport (Transport protocol, default RequestsTransport), clock (default SYSTEM_CLOCK), limiter (HostLimiter), quota (object with reserve(provider_id, host, *, priority) raising QuotaExceeded; default None), sanitizer (callable(source_id, content, content_type) -> bytes|None; default sanitize.sanitize_body), on_request_info (callable(RequestInfo)). Transport protocol: send(method, url, *, headers, body, timeout, max_bytes, deadline) -> Response for ONE hop (no redirect following, streamed with the size cap, deadline checked between chunks -> DeadlineExceeded for slow-drip servers). RequestsTransport: per-thread requests.Session (trust_env as configured), verify = settings ca_bundle or True (never False, A12), allow_redirects=False, stream=True.
 request(method, url, *, params, headers, data, json_body, timeout, ttl, allow_redirects=True, max_bytes, min_interval, user_agent, source='', provider='', hop_check=None, retries=None, deadline=None, cancel_event=None, cache_if=None, module='', opsec='passive', priority='seed') does: (a) provider = registry provider of source/provider, else provider_for_host(host); profile application: User-Agent from the profile (None/'neutral' -> settings user_agent 'V3LUM/<version>'; 'contact' -> 'V3LUM/<version> (+<contact_email>)'; a template with {version}/{contact}; 'browser' -> settings ua_light; a profile needing contact while contact_email is empty -> ConfigError) unless the caller set User-Agent; Accept / Accept-Language from the profile when not set by the caller (the hard-coded Accept-Language default is removed); timeout/retries/max_bytes/ttl/concurrency from the profile; politeness interval = max(min_interval, profile.min_interval); LIGHT/ACTIVE requests (opsec != passive) use settings ua_light, never the V3LUM/contact UA; (b) cache_key(method, url, body, *, accept='', credential_hash='') adds Accept and a sha256 of credential-bearing header values and key-like params (P326 cond 10); effective ttl = min(requested or profile ttl, cache_max_age_days*86400, retention_days*86400), and <= 7 days for sensitive providers; (c) offline mode unchanged; (d) quota.reserve(provider, host, priority=priority) before sending when installed; cancel_event set -> Cancelled; deadline passed -> DeadlineExceeded; timeout = min(timeout, remaining); (e) own redirect loop: <= 5 hops for 301/302/303/307/308 when allow_redirects (303 -> GET without body); hop_check(url) called before every hop (PolicyError stops); credential headers (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key, Api-Key, Auth-Key, Key, X-Auth-Token, Token and any header whose value is a registered secret) stripped when the host changes; https->http downgrade -> PolicyError('policy'); Response.history = hop URLs; (f) retries: 502/503/504 and connection errors retried at most `retries` times with clock.sleep backoff, never past the deadline; 429 retried once only when Retry-After <= 15 s and within the deadline, otherwise returned; a classified block/challenge/403 is never retried; (g) classify() every final response (markers = provider markers + caller markers) before caching; classified, truncated and 401/403/429/5xx responses are never cached (negative results only in memory); cache_if(resp) False -> not cached; for providers flagged sensitive the body passes the sanitizer hook before cache.put and before being returned (None -> no-store; the module gets the sanitized body when a schema exists, else the raw body in memory only); (h) a host classified challenge or geo_block is short-circuited for the client's lifetime: later requests raise Blocked(reason_code 'circuit') without sending (in memory only); (i) events: on_request(method, redacted_url, status, elapsed, cached, error) as today plus on_request_info(RequestInfo(ts, method, url (redacted), host, path (redacted), status, bytes, elapsed, cached, error, module, provider, source, opsec, egress_profile='default', resolved_ip='', port, classification)). Every URL or message leaving HttpClient (events, exceptions, cache url column) passes redact.redact_url/redact_text.
6. ScopedHttp: ScopedHttp(client, ttl=None, min_interval=0.0, user_agent=None) keeps working for any client exposing request(method, url, **kw) (tests/test_dns.py wraps FakeHttp directly); new keyword args module='', provider='', sources=(), allowed_hosts=None (None = no host check), disclosure='third_party', opsec='passive', max_requests=None, absent_statuses=frozenset(), error_markers=(), keyless=False, deadline=None, cancel_event=None, clock=None, core=False (core DoH scope: not counted, no module defaults), priority='seed'. Methods request/get/head/post(url, *, params, headers, data, json_body, timeout, ttl, allow_redirects=True, max_bytes, source='', cache_if=None, retries=None, **kw), get_json(url, *, absent=None, ok404=False, **kw) (None only for statuses in absent_statuses | absent; ok404=True means absent={404}), post_json(...), check(resp) (classify with the scope's markers and keyless flag, then raise_for_status), evict(resp) (deletes the cache row of that request). Enforcement: cancel -> Cancelled; deadline -> DeadlineExceeded; max_requests reached -> RequestCapReached (network sends only; cache hits free); host checks (P327 cond 4-5, A8 BR9) on the first request and on every redirect hop via hop_check: disclosure 'none' -> PolicyError('policy', 'offline module: no network'); passive third_party/internal -> URL host must match allowed_hosts (exact, or '*.suffix' for strict subdomains) else PolicyError('policy'); target modules may reach target-derived hosts (scope checks in wave 2). Counters requests, cache_hits, hosts (host -> network sends), bytes, request_log (list[RequestInfo] of this scope).
7. v3lum/core/redact.py (new, AR01): register_secret(value, label='') (values shorter than 6 chars ignored; thread-safe), registered_count(), clear() (tests); KEY_PARAMS = ('key','apikey','api_key','api-key','token','access_token','auth','auth_key','sig','signature','password','passwd','secret','client_secret'); redact_url(url) masks values of KEY_PARAMS query params and every registered secret anywhere in path/query/fragment (abuse.ch v2 export URLs embed the Auth-Key in the path); redact_text(text) masks registered secrets and key-like params inside URLs; redact_headers(headers) masks credential headers; MASK = '***'.
8. v3lum/core/net.py (new, thin; WP11 completes it in wave 2 with the same signatures): Connector(*, module='', disclosure='target', opsec=Opsec.LIGHT, deadline=None, cancel_event=None, clock=None) with connect(host, port, *, timeout=None) -> socket.socket (socket.create_connection; PolicyError for modules whose disclosure is not 'target'; honours cancel/deadline) and wrap_tls(sock, server_hostname, *, timeout=None) -> ssl.SSLSocket (default verifying context; verification never disabled). The only sanctioned socket source for modules (ctx.net).
9. tests/test_http.py (existing, local 127.0.0.1 server): keep every case; update only the assertions whose behaviour changed on purpose (default UA, Accept-Language, redirect history built by the own loop).
10. Review additions: HttpClient(..., cache_key_sink=None) calls cache_key_sink(cache_key) for every response written to or served from the cache (the engine collects them per case for the A10 purge); the quota protocol is reserve(provider_id, host, *, priority) plus signal(provider_id, *, kind ('quota'|'rate_limited'), until=None), called when a response is classified quota or rate_limited so the provider's own signal wins over the counters (P334 cond 8); HttpClient.circuit_hosts() -> frozenset[str] and reset_circuit() (the engine resets the circuit at the start of each investigate(); policy reads circuit_hosts() for POL-16); Accept-Language defaults to 'pt-BR,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.5' for hosts under .br when the profile sets none (P326 cond 11); user_agent templates accept only {version}, {contact}, {contact_url} and {app}, and a template whose setting is empty raises ConfigError (SKIPPED 'config', P326 cond 4).

Selection through policy: Engine builds one PolicyContext per investigate() (policy.make_context) and select(entity, *, run) -> (runnable: list[(cls, Decision)], blocked: list[(cls, Decision)]) calls policy.decide for every candidate (accepts filter, include/exclude/categories as today; preset 'deep' or include_disabled = every ready module through the gates; -M never bypasses a gate). 2. RunInfo per (module, entity): is_seed (node.seed and the seed was typed, not text-derived), depth, provenance (first-discovery edges up to the seed), allowed_sources from the Decision, tlp = entity TLP, deadline = clock.monotonic() + cls.timeout, priority ('seed' for depth 0, 'pivot' for depth 1, 'pivot2' deeper), internal_seed (seed resolves to private space and was typed).

Same-wave sibling names are used exactly as named in this plan (intra-wave protocol, wave-1 goal). 1. Egress profiles (P376 cond 1-4, A13) in v3lum/core/net.py: EgressProfiles(config) with 'default' (setting proxy: third-party APIs and DoH), 'light' (proxy_light) and 'active' (proxy_active); session_for(opsec, *, tags=()) -> (profile_name, requests.Session): every third-party API call and PASSIVE request -> default (never proxy_light/active); LIGHT -> light when configured, else default (the policy guard refuses hostile contact from the default route); ACTIVE -> active when configured, else default. Non-default profiles get their own requests.Session with trust_env=False, explicit proxies, no netrc; names resolved through the profile (socks5h:// via optional PySocks; HTTP CONNECT proxies resolve remotely); no local getaddrinfo for target hosts on non-default profiles. Fail closed: a configured profile whose proxy is unreachable -> PolicyError(reason_code 'policy', 'proxy_light unreachable: request refused'), never resent on the default route. Tor (socks5h to a Tor port, detected by setting or .onion use) allowed only as proxy_light; configured as proxy_active -> refused at load. Every RequestInfo carries egress_profile; public_ip(profile) via the benign echo service https://api.ipify.org?format=json (provider fragment ipify.json, tier trusted, flags false, source echo 'open'), on request only (doctor --egress, wave 5).
2. Connector v2 (same signatures as wave 1): sockets only through the module's profile (PySocks socksocket for socks5h), scope and SSRF checks after resolution, ceilings (ACTIVE <= 10 probes/s and <= 2 concurrent per target host via HostLimiter; port scans <= 1000 TCP ports, no UDP sweeps, <= 100 packets/s total unless scope limits.max_pps raises it (max 1000)), per-case ACTIVE budget 10000 probes/requests unless scope limits.max_requests (<= 50000), wordlists capped at 5000 entries (Connector.cap_wordlist(seq)), cancel within 2 s, every connection emitted as a RequestInfo (method 'CONNECT') for the ledger.
3. SSRF/redirect guard (AR02) through the hop_check installed by ScopedHttp: each hop's host is resolved through the request's profile resolver and refused (PolicyError 'policy') when any resolved IP is private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, ULA fc00::/7, multicast/reserved or cloud metadata (169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254), or when the name is single-label or ends with .local/.internal/.lan/.corp/.home/.intranet/.localdomain - unless RunInfo.internal_seed is set or the scope lists it; on the direct route the checked IP is pinned for the connection (custom urllib3 connection to the checked IP with SNI/Host = name); with an HTTP CONNECT proxy the name is sent and the profile resolver's answer is the checked set (limitation documented by WP29 in docs/OPSEC.md). Target requests (LIGHT/ACTIVE) are scope-checked at connection time and on every redirect hop (out of scope -> PolicyError 'scope'); LIGHT/ACTIVE contact re-runs policy.contact_guard for redirect targets.
4. v3lum/core/scope.py (A7): Scope.load(path) (TOML via tomllib, or JSON) with {authorization_ref, owner, contacts[], ticket, window_start, window_end (UTC ISO), targets {domains[] (exact or '*.' wildcard), cidrs[], url_prefixes[]}, exclusions {domains, cidrs, url_prefixes}, shared_infra_hosts[], limits {max_rps, max_concurrency, max_pps (<= 1000), max_requests (<= 50000)}, roe {user_agent, header {name, value}}}; validate(authorization_ref, now) -> list[str] (mismatch, outside window, malformed, limits above ceilings); sha256; matches_host(host), matches_ip(ip), matches_url(url) (exclusions win); allows_contact(host, ips, *, probe='http'|'network') -> (bool, reason): resolved private/... Stage order: sanitize.scrub_text (combos dropped, secrets masked) -> decode layers (depth <= 3: plausible base64 blocks, quoted-printable, URL-encoding, HTML entities; decoded output <= 2x input and <= 20 MB; embedded archives never decompressed) -> refang (patterns adapted from ninoseki ioc-extractor and ioc-fanger, MIT, with attribution headers and notice fragments) -> span-masked extraction (URLs first, then e-mails, then domains outside URL/e-mail spans, IPs, hashes, CVE/ATT&CK, crypto) -> validation (ipaddress; IANA TLD + PSL; P217 checksums - an MD5-looking string is never BTC; ATT&CK ids via attack.is_valid; CVE years 1999..current+1; bogon/private IPs kept but flagged; file-extension TLDs (.zip .mov .py .sh .md ...) low confidence unless defanged, with a scheme or resolving) -> warninglist annotation (noise kinds) -> pivot. Flags: 'bogon', 'private', 'low_confidence_tld', 'warninglisted', 'org_domain', 'recipient_token', 'personal', 'secret'. Brazilian scam text (cond 6): national phones without '+' ((11) 98765-4321, 11 98765-4321, 0800) validated against v3lum/data/anatel_ddd.json; wa.me/<digits> and api.whatsapp.com/send?phone= -> phone; t.me/<name> -> telegram_handle; t.me/+<invite> and t.me/joinchat/ -> telegram_invite; discord.gg/ -> discord_invite; instagram/tiktok/x/facebook profile URLs -> social_account; PIX BR Code (000201...6304+CRC) -> pix_brcode (handed to P233 modules); 14-digit CNPJ with a valid DV. Privacy (cond 7-8, AR24): CPFs are masked and never become entities (counted with a masked preview), card numbers become payment_card (BIN6…last4), secrets become secret entities (fingerprints) reported once as 'sensitive data in pasted text'; PERSONAL_TYPES flagged 'personal' (the engine does not auto-expand them); org-profile domains, the sender's own domain and warninglisted values flagged; URLs carrying an org e-mail (plain, URL-encoded, base64) flagged 'recipient_token' (never fetched automatically). Static and offline (disclosure 'none'): files never rendered, remote templates/UNC paths/URLs/images never resolved. The 5000-IOC limit is reported when hit.
2. v3lum/core/detect.py: extract_iocs(text, limit=5000) becomes a thin wrapper returning [e.entity for e in ioc.extract(text, limit=limit).entities] (tests/test_detect.py unchanged and green); detect() keeps today's precedence (P323 cond 1) and adds single-value detection of the new types only from an explicit TYPE:value prefix, a URL pattern (t.me/, discord.gg/, discord.com/invite/, bsky.app/profile/, steamcommunity.com/) or an unambiguous structure (header block -> email_headers; 'T1' + 70 hex -> tlsh; leading '@user@instance' -> fediverse_handle), never from bare hex or digit length (P333 cond 4); email_headers parsing is static (no remote images, pixels, CSS or links; recipient lists not pivoted).
3. v3lum/core/patterns.py (new, P323): Pattern(name, kind ('secret'|'financial'|'identifier'|'crypto'|'analytics'|'srv'|'header'), regex, validator, confidence, enabled, consumer, vectors_ok, vectors_bad); PATTERNS imported from lemmeknow/pywhat regex.json and the SpiderFoot offline extractors (MIT, attributed) restricted to patterns with a validator or distinctive prefix/checksum (AWS/GCP/Azure/GitHub/Slack/Stripe-secret keys, JWT, crypto with checksum, analytics ids, IBAN with mod-97, cards with Luhn, SRV names, odd headers); generic patterns (phone, date, generic ids) disabled; no validator -> confidence <= 0.5; patterns without a consuming module and no masking need are not emitted; every regex has a pathological-input test (ReDoS review). Financial and secret hits are local-only findings: no pivots, never passed to third_party/target modules, masked in terminal, reports, evidence and case DB (cond 5-7); detection-triggered DNS lookups (if any) obey the TLP gate (cond 8).
4. v3lum/modules/utility/ioc_extract.py: thin wrapper over ioc.extract (span/line kept in pivot notes as provenance; preview finding '37 IOCs: 12 domains, 5 IPs, 4 low-confidence'), metadata unchanged from WP06.

Review additions: detect() and ioc.extract consult the actor/malware alias index - fragments v3lum/data/aliases/*.json (schema 'v3lum.aliases/1': {kind: 'malware_family'|'threat_actor', source, licence, names: {alias: canonical}}; the P295 batch ships the data, the README is written here) - so known malware/actor names are typed malware_family/threat_actor (confidence 0.8) instead of username (AR18); social_account detection uses entities.platform_for_url() over the merged platform fragments (WP05); ioc.extract and the aliases schema are documented in docs/contract_additions/WP17.md.

packages.title: Risk model v2 (P302: severity x confidence x Admiralty reliability x MISP decay x asset criticality, noisy-OR with ceilings) and display grouping (P335)
packages.spec:
CONTRACT FREEZE (A16): docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md v2 and every name listed in module_author_contract are frozen since wave 1; this package must not rename them or change their documented behaviour (additions only; any breaking change needs an architect-approved migration). Module-facing additions (new ctx/core names, fragment schemas, reserved tags) are documented in docs/contract_additions/<this package id>.md, owned by the package that adds them; docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md itself is never edited after the freeze (link fixes by WP29 only). Same-wave sibling names are used exactly as named in this plan (intra-wave protocol, wave-1 goal). 1. v3lum/core/scoring.py (pure function, documented constants, every P302 final condition): W_SEV = {CRITICAL: 10, HIGH: 7, MEDIUM: 4, LOW: 2, INFO: 0}; C_CONF = Confidence.weight; R_SRC prior = providers.ADMIRALTY[grade of the finding's source provider] (A 1.0, B 0.85, C 0.7, D 0.5, E 0.3, F 0.5), replaced by store.source_reliability() values (>= 5 votes, floor 0.3) when given; DECAY = MISP polynomial base x (1 - (t/tau)^(1/delta)) with TAU_DAYS = {'ip': 30, 'url': 30, 'domain': 90, 'typosquat': 180, 'breach': 1095, 'infostealer': 365, 'hash': None} and DELTA = 1.0, t from Finding.observed_last (tag/type selects the class); no timestamp -> no decay and label 'age unknown'; A_CRIT = {'critical': 1.0, 'high': 0.95, 'medium': 0.85, 'low': 0.6}, default 1.0. Per-finding weight = W_sev/10 x C_conf x R_src x decay x A_crit; contributions deduplicated per (entity, tag family, upstream family) and combined by noisy-OR, capped at 100; severity ceiling: an entity or case level never exceeds the highest severity among its contributing findings and correlations (weak signals escalate only through a correlation rule); correlations take the max/uplift over the findings they cite, never a second noisy-OR term; '+1 confidence level' only with >= 2 independent upstream families; case score = seeds + correlations + the top-5 pivot entities weighted by Node.path_confidence; shared-infrastructure relations (co-hosted, same ASN, same NS/MX, CDN) cap the transferred contribution at LOW; own assets and known-good/verified entities (tags known_good, verified_fi; gov.br) never inherit risk from neighbours; warninglisted findings count as POSSIBLE with a label; licence-disabled sources contribute nothing. LEVELS keep thresholds 80/55/30/8 and rename the lowest level 'no findings'; seeds with fewer than 2 reputation-capable sources answering (case['answered']) are listed as inconclusive. score(graph, correlations, reliability=None, *, source_reliability=None, now=None, coverage=None) keeps the v1 positional signature and the v1 keys score/level/entities/top, and adds contributors (top-3 for the case: finding_id, entity, path, confidence_label, weight, words), label 'triage aid, not a conclusion', inconclusive (seed keys), no_export (PERSONAL_TYPES entity keys: their scores are never exported to STIX/MISP as person scores and never drive automated actions), model 'v3lum.risk/2'.
The module docstring's stale reference to v3lum.core.feedback is replaced by the real Store feedback API (AR22 docs test). 2. v3lum/core/engine.py: _finish passes source_reliability (Engine(..., source_reliability=...) supplied by App from Store.source_reliability()), now=runtime.now() and coverage=case.coverage/answered; nothing else in the engine changes.
3. v3lum/core/grouping.py (P335, presentation only; JSON/STIX/MISP keep every finding): normalize_url_key(url) (lower-case host without www./m., no trailing slash, tracking params utm_*, fbclid, gclid, igshid, ref, si, hl, trk dropped, remaining query sorted; URLs without a path never group); group_findings(findings: list[dict]) -> list[FindingGroup(key, member_ids, severity (max), confidence_label (max) and its criterion, count, sources, upstream_families)] via union-find over: the same breach name across sources, URL variants of one resource, the same CVE from several sources; identity entities (username, social_account, person_name, email, phone) are never merged; group_correlations(correlations) by entity; keys deterministic and documented in the module docstring.

Review additions: v3lum/app.py (only the Engine construction in App.scan and App.run_single): Engine(rt, options, reliability=self.store.reliability(), source_reliability=self.store.source_reliability(), overrides=self.store.overrides_for); Engine._finish applies the analyst overrides (Finding.apply_override for every finding id returned by overrides(ids)) before the WP08 suppression stage, correlations and scoring, so analyst decisions win and survive re-runs (P322 cond 3, P258 cond 3/12); scoring ignores findings tagged context_only (A4 BR6/BR9, P146 cond 7) and builds its inconclusive list from answered[seed].reputation_answered < 2.

2. Alerts (cond 7-10): only for NEW registrable domains, deduplicated by registrable domain + certificate serial; one terminal line each with the reason it matched, a JSONL record (timestamp, rule id, matched name, registrable domain, reason, cert sha256, issuer, not_before) in ~/.v3lum/watch/alerts-<date>.jsonl (0600) and an alerts table row; certificate metadata only; above 200 alerts per hour one summary line replaces the rest; mutes per rule and per domain (watch_mutes table; `watch mute`/`unmute`); per-rule precision from P325 votes; hits only enqueue capped passive enrichment through the policy gate (<= setting watch_enrich_per_hour (30) per hour; the rest listed for the analyst); never automatic LIGHT/ACTIVE contact; alerts and first_seen state follow retention_days and the TLP (default AMBER). Ransomware victim watch only with the ransomware.live PRO key and only victim metadata (leaked files never downloaded); Telegram public-channel watch only as delivered by P357 (module batch) under its own conditions.
3. commands/watch.py: `v3lum watch [--once] [--max-runtime SECONDS] [--max-alerts N] [--tlp LEVEL]`, `watch rules` (list rules derived from the profile), `watch mute <rule|domain>`, `watch unmute ...`; doctor shows CertStream reachability and polling-source status (data exposed via watch.health()).

packages.title: Web access-log input (P340, scope extension): streaming parser, offline teler-resources/PHPIDS matching, privacy-preserving aggregation
packages.spec: CONTRACT FREEZE: docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md (contract v2) is frozen; this package only ADDS names (document them in docs/contract_additions/WP31.md). The team lead extended the build scope to every approved P3 item, so P340 (previously deferred) is implemented here, following every P340 final condition (core_G15.md). 1. v3lum/core/weblog.py: streaming parser for Apache/Nginx combined and common log formats, IIS W3C extended logs and JSON-lines access logs (format sniffed from the first lines); the file is never read whole; line length cap 8 KB (longer lines counted and skipped); size and line caps (settings weblog_max_bytes default 2 GB, weblog_max_lines default 5,000,000) reported when hit; progress callback; 1M lines parse in < 30 s offline (perf test with a generated file, marked so it can be skipped on slow CI only via an explicit env var, never silently). 2. Matching: teler-resources web-attack patterns and bad-crawler lists (CC BY 4.0, attributed) and PHPIDS filters (LGPL-3.0 data, used unmodified) registered with the dataset manager v2 (register_dataset with licence/terms_class/attribution/pinned or validated content), downloaded at runtime by `v3lum data update`, never bundled (A6); compiled once per run; patterns that show catastrophic backtracking on the pathological-line test corpus are excluded (and listed in doctor). If P317 user_agent_analysis (module batch) already ships a teler-resources loader, reuse it from there via a small shared function in weblog.py and keep one loader (P340 cond 2). Provider fragments v3lum/data/providers/teler_resources.json and phpids.json record terms (open: CC BY 4.0 / LGPL data with attribution) and tier. 3. Aggregation per client IP / path / UA before any pivot; only IPs that matched attack signatures or bad-crawler lists become IPV4/IPV6 entities, capped at the top 20 by suspicious hits (setting weblog_max_ip_pivots); benign visitors are counted, never stored. 4. Private/internal IPs and hostnames never leave the machine (no pivots for them); URLs lose their query string before any external lookup; stored request lines have query-string values redacted and no cookies; evidence keeps the matched lines (redacted) and the log file's SHA-256, never a copy of the file. 5. Log-derived IP pivots get passive enrichment only (the engine never schedules LIGHT/ACTIVE for them: mark provenance so policy refuses target contact). 6. Cases created from a log default to TLP:AMBER. 7. v3lum/modules/file_analysis/web_access_log.py: the module (disclosure 'none', terms 'open', opsec PASSIVE, default_enabled True per the chair decision, accepts the file input type the core already uses for file analysis; applies() only when weblog sniffing recognises an access log) producing the aggregate facts, matched-rule findings (severity by rule class and hit counts, confidence labels per P322) and the capped IP pivots. 8. detect.py: recognise an access-log file path/content as the file input with a 'web_access_log' hint (no new entity type unless the existing file type cannot carry it). 9. ui/render.py: the first screen for a log case is a summary ('312 IPs, 14 matched rules, top 10 IPs by hits, paths attacked').

module_author_contract:
MODULE-AUTHOR CONTRACT v2 (frozen at the end of wave 1 in docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md; later waves may only ADD names, never rename or change behaviour - A16).

0. SEQUENCING AND MERGE GATES (what authors can rely on and when)
- From wave 1 on: every name below exists with a working implementation; module files, tests, fixtures and data fragments may be added (authors never edit shared core files).
- Enforcement that arrives later without changing names: policy gate + licence/TLP/tier/privacy/own-asset/scope/egress gates (wave 2, WP07/WP08), full sanitizer stage + forbidden-capability lint (wave 2, WP09), provider quotas (wave 2, WP10), egress/SSRF/scope (wave 2, WP11), declarative-spec compiler (wave 2, WP12), evidence/audit (wave 3), data rules P301 (wave 4), safety suite AR20 (wave 5), golden-path harness AR21 (wave 5).
- Merge gate per module (A16): registry contract test green (tests/test_registry_contract.py), trimmed real fixtures without personal data, offline tests with tests/fakes.py (unmatched requests fail, network guard active), a provider-registry entry for every host and feed, the P327 lint (from wave 2). A source module counts as default only through the policy gate (wave 2). LIGHT/ACTIVE module files must not be added before tests/safety/test_scope.py exists (WP28, wave 5): the contract test fails otherwise (A7 merge gate). Per group, the AR21 golden-path fixtures go to tests/fixtures/acceptance/<type>/<module>.json (format below). Until the policy gate lands (wave 2) source modules (disclosure third_party/internal/target) run only when selected explicitly (interim A16 BR5 guard). Module-facing additions after the freeze are documented per package in docs/contract_additions/<package>.md (additions only): sanitize.scrub_text and the lint API (WP09), ctx.net.run_tool with core/tools.py ToolSpec for external binaries (WP11; LIGHT/ACTIVE only), ioc.extract and the aliases index (WP17), data rules 'v3lum.rule/1' (WP22), tls.check_interception (WP25), the watch-source invocation (WP26).

1. MODULE CLASS (v3lum/core/module.py; one file per module under v3lum/modules/<category>/, auto-discovered, decorated with @register)
Identity: name (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,63}$, unique), title, description, category (one of CATEGORIES, unchanged 21 keys), reference (docs/terms URL), tags (free; reserved: core, offline, slow, noisy, brazil, free, curated_pack, cached_only, high_fp, bulk_download, people_sweep, sensitive_sites, fresh_assessment, cert_derived, pack, reputation (the module returns a malicious/suspicious/benign verdict for its accepted IOC types: counts for 'inconclusive', the A3 minimum answer set and doctor), watch_source (polling source invoked by `v3lum watch` on org-profile rule entities; reports new names in attribute watch_hits), watch_only (never selected outside `v3lum watch`); module.RESERVED_TAGS maps each reserved tag to its meaning), notice.
Inputs/outputs: accepts (non-empty set of EntityType), produces (set of EntityType), run_on: 'any' (default) | 'seeds' (analyst-typed seeds only) | 'own_assets' (per-person breach/stealer: verified org domains, or --breach-scope all + purpose on typed seeds) | 'own_assets_only' (txt_verified/attested org entries only); applies(entity, ctx) -> bool hook (unchanged).
MUST be declared in the class body (registration refuses otherwise): terms ('open' | 'key-terms' | 'license' | 'noncommercial' | 'unknown'; base default 'unknown'), opsec (Opsec.PASSIVE | LIGHT | ACTIVE), disclosure ('none' | 'internal' | 'third_party' | 'target'; no default), hosts (tuple of exact hosts or '*.suffix' wildcards; () for none/target/DoH-only modules); when disclosure != 'none' also max_requests and expected_latency.
Other ClassVars (defaults): provider='' (primary provider id; required for third_party/internal), sources=() (fully qualified registry source ids 'provider.source'; required for third_party/internal; offline dataset users list their dataset sources), access_model ('free_noauth_unlimited' | 'free_noauth_limited' | 'free_auth_limited' | 'free_auth_unlimited' | 'commercial_only' | 'internal' | 'offline'; required for third_party; default 'offline' for none, 'internal' for internal, 'free_noauth_unlimited' for target), requires_keys=(), optional_keys=(), requires_packages=() (import names; only packages in module.OPTIONAL_PACKAGES, which merges the core extras with fragments v3lum/data/extras/<package>.json ('v3lum.extra/1': {package, pip, extra, licence, justification}) - a batch adds a fragment and never edits pyproject.toml), max_requests=10 (HTTP requests via ctx.http per entity per run, 0..100000; DoH not counted), expected_latency=5.0 (declared p50 seconds), timeout=60.0 (run deadline), min_interval=0.0, max_rate=None (LIGHT <= 1.0, ACTIVE <= 10.0 req/s per target host), daily_quota=None (fallback when the provider has no quota block), cache_ttl=None, max_pivots=100, requires_egress=frozenset() (ISO alpha-2, e.g. {'BR'}), absent_statuses=frozenset() (documented meaningful absences, e.g. {404}), error_markers=() (same schema as provider error markers), manual_link='' ('<pack>:<link_id>' or an inline https template with link placeholders; emitted when automation is skipped/blocked), default_enabled=True (candidate flag only: it can lower, never force, the effective default set), settings={} (module-scoped settings name -> default; readable via ctx.setting, settable via `v3lum config set`; names unique across modules and core).
health_check (classmethod) -> HealthCheck(etype, value, expect='ok', offline=False, selftest=None) | None. Default: None for disclosure 'none'; the first accepted type found in module.BENIGN_VALUES (example.com, https://example.com/, someone@example.com, 8.8.8.8, 2001:4860:4860::8888, 8.8.8.0/24, AS15169, EICAR md5/sha1/sha256, CVE-2021-44228, octocat) otherwise. LIGHT/ACTIVE modules MUST override with HealthCheck(offline=True, selftest=callable) (offline self-test, loopback only). selftest is callable(ctx) -> HealthResult(status 'ok'|'blocked'|'quota'|'needs_key'|'dead', detail=''); with offline=True the ctx has no network beyond loopback, with offline=False it is a normal passive ctx (packs sampling their sites, e.g. username claimed/unclaimed checks).
Removed in v2 (declaring them fails registration): user_agent (use the provider http_profile), shares_input (derived), and every derived name of section 2.
Registration (@register) refuses, with a fix hint, any module failing: identity/enums; MUST-declare; opsec LIGHT/ACTIVE <=> disclosure 'target'; disclosure 'none' => hosts==() and provider==''; 'internal' => provider internal=true; 'third_party' => registered provider and sources, every host owned by a provider of the module's sources; terms == most restrictive class of its sources (open < key-terms < license < noncommercial < unknown; no sources => disclosure none/target and terms 'open'); max_rate ceilings; requires_egress codes; absent_statuses 100-599; error_markers schema; manual_link resolvable; settings collisions; A3 default rule (default_enabled MUST be False for LIGHT/ACTIVE, terms unknown, tier unknown, max_requests > 10 without tag curated_pack, expected_latency > 10, category person_name with disclosure third_party, tags high_fp/bulk_download/people_sweep/sensitive_sites/fresh_assessment, fetches_target providers without tag cached_only); sensitive modules need a sanitizer schema for every source; requires_keys/optional_keys registered; requires_packages known. Failures never crash the tool: they appear in module.load_errors() (the contract test requires none).
readiness_check(cls, keys, mode, authorized=False) -> Readiness(ready, status, reason_code, reason); readiness() legacy wrapper; describe() keeps every v1 key and adds the v2 fields.

2. DERIVED ATTRIBUTES (set by @register from the provider registry; never declared): trust_tier ('trusted'|'community'|'unknown'; 'n/a' for none/internal/target), providers (frozenset), upstream_families, reliability (Admiralty A-F of the primary provider), sensitive (category breach_leak or any sensitive provider), publishes_queries, reuses_queries, fetches_target, shares_input (= disclosure in {third_party, target}), max_tlp (tlp.max_tlp: none/internal -> RED; target -> AMBER (RED only for verified own assets not third_party_hosted); trusted -> AMBER+STRICT; community -> AMBER; unknown or reuses_queries -> GREEN; publishes_queries -> never), access_label (plain words), terms_sources.

3. STATUSES, REASON CODES, PARTIAL RUNS (v3lum/core/models.py)
Status: ok, empty, error, skipped, needs_key, rate_limited, blocked, unavailable (unchanged) + quota (budget/daily/monthly limit, distinct from transient rate_limited).
REASON_CODES (A3 canonical, the only codes): SKIPPED: not_default, demoted, licence, tlp, tier, privacy, own_asset, opsec, authorization, scope, egress_country, deadline, policy, config, not_applicable | NEEDS_KEY: needs_key | UNAVAILABLE: package, dataset, offline | QUOTA: quota | RATE_LIMITED: rate_limited | BLOCKED: hostile_host, circuit, challenge (anti-bot/WAF challenge, keyless HTTP 403, DNSBL refusal), geo_block, login_wall | ERROR: timeout, sanitizer, error. DEFAULT_REASON per status; status_for(code); valid_reason(status, code).
Partial runs keep status ok/empty with ModuleResult.partial=True and stop_reason in STOP_REASONS = {request_cap, deadline, quota, rate_limited, cancelled}. The engine recovers the result a module was building when ctx.http raises RequestCapReached/Cancelled/QuotaExceeded/RateLimited mid-run (models.collect_results), so modules simply let these exceptions propagate.
Rule 5 everywhere: 403/429/challenges/timeouts/SERVFAIL mean "could not verify", never "absent"; never write 'not found', 'not listed', 'no account', 'clean' or 'does not exist' for a source that did not answer.
Exception -> status mapping done by the engine: QuotaExceeded -> quota; RateLimited -> rate_limited; Blocked -> blocked (+ its reason_code); AuthRequired -> needs_key for keyed modules, blocked/challenge for keyless; OfflineError -> unavailable/offline; DatasetUnavailable -> unavailable/dataset; PolicyError -> skipped (+ reason_code, default policy); ConfigError -> skipped/config; DeadlineExceeded -> error/timeout; NetworkError/HttpError/other -> error/error; sanitizer failure -> error/sanitizer (raw dropped). applies() False -> skipped/not_applicable.

4. CONFIDENCE (P322): Confidence.CONFIRMED / PROBABLE / POSSIBLE ('confirmed','probable','possible'); weights 1.0/0.7/0.4 (scoring), STIX 90/70/40; Confidence.from_value(float|str) with >= 0.85 confirmed, >= 0.55 probable, else possible. criterion (text) is MANDATORY for severity >= low (strict mode raises ContractViolation in tests). Automatic downgrades only through named suppression rules (Finding.downgrade(rule, reason) -> criterion 'POSSIBLE - on warninglist <name>'); upgrades at most +1 and only with >= 2 independent upstream families (Finding.upgrade); analyst overrides always win (stored separately by deterministic finding id). Pivot edges carry the same labels.

5. RESULT AND FINDING HELPERS (ModuleResult, built with self.result(entity))
- res.finding(title, severity='info', description='', *, confidence=0.8|'probable', criterion='', data=None, tags=(), references=(), source='', observed_first=None, observed_last=None, attack=(), key='') -> Finding. Finding.id = sha256('module|entity.key|title|key')[:16] (deterministic: keep titles stable, put counts in description/data, use key= to separate same-title findings). source = registry source id; observed_first/observed_last = provider timestamps (ISO-8601; drive decay; omit when unknown). attack = ATT&CK ids validated against data/attack.
- res.pivot(etype, value, relation, *, confidence=0.9|label, expand=True, note='') -> Entity|None (invalid values dropped).
- res.attr(key, value) (vocabulary names only); res.link(label, url) (http/https only; others dropped).
- res.mark(status, error='', *, reason_code='') -> res (default reason per status; validated).
- res.stop(stop_reason) -> res (partial=True).
- res.presence(state, *, marker='', url='', checked_at=None, source='') with state found|absent|unknown (tri-state existence; 'absent' needs a marker or URL as positive evidence) -> attribute 'presence'.
- res.set_marking(tlp) (results carrying a platform marking raise the entity/case TLP, A12).
- res.source_status(source_id, status, *, reason_code='', reason='') (aggregators: per-feed outcome of one of the module's sources, e.g. a blocked or rate-limited feed while the others answered); feeds outside ctx.allowed_sources are reported by the engine automatically (reason_code 'licence').
- res.raw (saved as sanitized evidence), res.reason_code, res.partial, res.stop_reason, res.tlp; res.hosts / res.datasets / res.redacted_fields are filled by the engine.
- Secrets: never put raw secrets anywhere; use sanitize.mask_secret(raw, kind) -> {type, preview first4…last4, sha256} or entities.secret_entity(kind, raw); combos (email:password) are dropped by the core.
- Strict contract mode (V3LUM_STRICT=1, always on in tests): unknown vocab names, missing criterion, non-http(s) links and 'absent' without evidence raise.
- Analyst overrides: Finding.override / Finding.apply_override(*, label, severity, verdict, analyst, note, at) (set through `v3lum cases override|confirm`, applied by the engine on re-runs); Finding.downgrade(rule, reason, *, to=None) and Finding.upgrade() never cross an override. Finding tag context_only = shown as context, never scored (third-party breach context, generic/role/test addresses, anonymity networks).

6. CONTEXT (ctx, v3lum/core/context.py)
ctx.http (ScopedHttp), ctx.dns (Resolver), ctx.net (Connector, raw sockets for target modules only), ctx.data (DataView), ctx.org (OrgProfile), ctx.key(name), ctx.has_key(name), ctx.key_plan(name) ('business'|'free'|''), ctx.setting(name, default=None) (core + module settings), ctx.log(message, level='info'), ctx.cancelled(), ctx.now() (aware UTC; frozen in tests), ctx.remaining() (seconds to the run deadline or None), ctx.quota_remaining() (remaining provider/module budget or None), properties ctx.mode, ctx.authorized, ctx.options (ScanOptions), ctx.entity, ctx.is_seed (analyst-typed seed), ctx.depth, ctx.provenance (tuple of (parent_key, relation, module)), ctx.allowed_sources (frozenset of source ids the module may query in this run; aggregators MUST query only these - the engine reports the blocked rest - and use res.source_status for runtime per-feed failures), ctx.state (ModuleState: get/set/delete/all, persistent per-module JSON under ~/.v3lum/state/, 0600, 1 MB cap, never personal values or secrets - the only persistence a module may use), ctx.allowed_opsec (min(mode, module opsec)), ctx.tlp (entity TLP value 'clear'|'green'|'amber'|'amber+strict'|'red'), ctx.purpose, ctx.case_id, ctx.deadline. Modules never choose proxies, UAs or resolvers. ctx.dns uses a per-run core DoH scope: not counted in max_requests or quotas, but its hosts are listed in the disclosure ledger (res.hosts).

7. HTTP (v3lum/core/http.py)
ctx.http.get/head/post/request(url, *, params=None, headers=None, data=None, json_body=None, timeout=None, ttl=None, allow_redirects=True, max_bytes=None, source='', cache_if=None, retries=None) -> Response; ctx.http.get_json(url, *, absent=None, **kw) / post_json(...) -> parsed JSON, or None only when the status is in absent_statuses or absent (ok404=True is a deprecated alias of absent={404}); ctx.http.check(resp) -> resp (raises per classification; call it when parsing HTML/text yourself); ctx.http.evict(resp) (drop a cached response the module judged unusable); cache_if=callable(resp)->bool vetoes caching; counters requests, cache_hits, hosts, bytes, request_log.
Response: status, url (final), headers (lower-case), content, text, json(), ok, elapsed, from_cache, fetched_at (cache row time when from cache), truncated, history (hop URLs), request_url, host, source, classification, blocked (legacy reason), raise_for_status().
Exceptions (all importable from v3lum.core.http): HttpError(reason_code), RateLimited, AuthRequired, Blocked(reason_code challenge|geo_block|login_wall|circuit|hostile_host), QuotaExceeded, NetworkError, OfflineError, DeadlineExceeded, Cancelled, RequestCapReached, PolicyError(reason_code), ConfigError.
Core behaviour authors rely on: provider http_profile applied by host (UA, Accept, Accept-Language, timeout, retries, max_bytes, ttl, min_interval, concurrency; default UA neutral 'V3LUM/<version>'; contact UA only where the profile asks and contact_email is set, else SKIPPED/config); own redirect loop (<= 5 hops, every hop host-checked, credential headers stripped on host change, https->http refused); PASSIVE modules reach only their declared hosts (PolicyError -> SKIPPED/policy); disclosure 'none' modules get no network; max_requests -> RequestCapReached; run deadline/cancel -> DeadlineExceeded/Cancelled; one retry honouring Retry-After <= 15 s, never a retry with other UA/headers after a block; classified, 401/403/429/5xx and truncated responses are never cached; sensitive providers are cached only sanitized or not at all; all URLs/messages leaving the client are redacted (configured key values and key-like params masked).
Body-error classification (P321): http.classify(resp, *, markers=(), keyless=False) -> Classification(status 'blocked'|'rate_limited'|'quota'|'error', reason_code, reason, marker_id) | None, run on every response before parsing and caching: module/provider error markers, login-wall/geo-block/challenge final-URL and body fingerprints (weak captcha words only on error statuses), 429 -> rate_limited, keyless 403 -> blocked/challenge. Error marker schema (module error_markers and provider error_markers): {"id": str, "statuses": [200], "json_path": "a.b" | null, "equals": any, "regex": str | null, "final_url_regex": str | null, "maps_to": "blocked"|"rate_limited"|"quota"|"error", "reason_code": optional canonical code, "reason": "human text naming the provider"}.

8. DNS (v3lum/core/dns.py): ctx.dns.query(name, rtype='A', *, hostile=False) -> DnsAnswer(name, rtype, status, records, ttl, authenticated ('validated by resolver', never proof), error, resolver) with .ok, .nxdomain (only from a real NXDOMAIN answer), .nodata, .could_not_verify (SERVFAIL/REFUSED/TIMEOUT/transport errors); ctx.dns.ptr(ip); ctx.dns.addresses(name); ctx.dns.wildcard(zone) -> bool|None; ctx.dns.confirm_nxdomain(name, rtype='A') -> bool|None (second resolver; required before using NXDOMAIN for takeover/typosquat/'domain does not exist' decisions); ctx.dns.dnsbl(query_name, zone) -> DnsblResult(listed: bool|None, codes, status, reason) (never through public resolvers; refusal codes 127.255.255.x are blocked/rate_limited/error, never 'not listed').
